Through a network of directly operated stores and franchise member stores, it gathers real estate information and customer needs and uses them across its businesses.
entries.1fdd1df1a80c591c: A reportable segment in which the subsidiary Financial Do, in partnership with financial institutions, provides guarantees for reverse mortgages. A reverse mortgage is a loan for seniors that allows borrowing against collateral such as one's home, and the company handles real estate collateral appraisal and debt guarantees. It also offers real estate-secured loans to individuals and corporations that own real estate. For the fiscal year ended June 2026, sales were ¥630 million (up 12.9% from the previous year) and segment profit was ¥262 million (up 46.3%). Partner financial institutions increased to 55, new guarantees were 513 (up 1.8%), cumulative guarantees were 2,308, and the cumulative guaranteed balance was ¥35,344 million.

entries.de3294f94d262d47: For the fiscal year ended June 2026, gross profit was ¥10,771 million (down 25.9% year on year), selling, general and administrative expenses were ¥9,651 million (down 19.0%), and operating profit was ¥1,120 million (down 57.3%). Ordinary profit was ¥1,120 million (down 61.9%), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥1,452 million (down 38.0%). Extraordinary income included a gain on sale of shares in affiliated companies and other items. The annual securities report says the Real Estate Sales Business fell below its original plan, and that the rise in costs from upfront investment in personnel recruitment and the decline in earnings from shrinking and divested businesses could not be offset.

entries.e46ebca8d463b71c: This is a reporting segment in which subsidiary House Do Housing Sales expands the "House Do" brand real estate franchise nationwide. It provides know-how on brokerage of sales and leasing (customer attraction, IT, education and training, and other matters) to real estate businesses and to companies newly entering the real estate business from other industries. In the fiscal year ended June 2026, sales were ¥3,234 million (up 3.6% from the previous fiscal year) and segment profit was ¥1,928 million (up 0.4%). There were 121 new franchise agreements (down 3.2%) and 111 new store openings (up 32.1%), and as of June 30, 2026, the cumulative number of franchised stores was 733 and the cumulative number of opened stores was 637. It is stated that about 7-tenths of the franchised companies were companies that newly entered the real estate business from other industries.
entries.e934da35bcc5054e: Real Estate Sales Business: acquisition of real estate and sale with added value (revenue for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥35,219 million; 1,309 transactions)
entries.ead5c7ee349cfaaf: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] describes the company group as consisting of the company, five consolidated subsidiaries and one equity-method affiliate, which operate the Franchise Business, Real Estate Sales Business, Financial Business and House Leaseback Business. Its management philosophy is “We will be needed by customers and devote ourselves to them.” Under a five-year medium-term management plan with the fiscal year ending June 2030 as its final year, the company’s policy is to concentrate resources on the Franchise Business, Real Estate Sales Business and Financial Business, which have high growth potential and profitability. Revenue for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥49,617 million (down 23.4% year on year), operating profit was ¥1,120 million (down 57.3%), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥1,452 million (down 38.0%). Revenue of the [[term:segment|reportable segments]] was ¥35,219 million for the Real Estate Sales Business, ¥9,521 million for the House Leaseback Business, ¥3,234 million for the Franchise Business and ¥630 million for the Financial Business; in addition, “Other Business,” which is not included in the reportable segments, was ¥1,011 million.
entries.f1a7269a47024e2c: A reportable segment in which the Company and House Do Japan, mainly at "house and real estate buyout specialty stores," acquire items such as used houses for buyout, renovation and resale, newly built detached houses for sale, residential land for development, and whole-building income-generating properties, add value, and sell them. Among the reportable segments, it has the largest sales to external customers. For the fiscal year ended June 2026, sales were ¥35,219 million (down 10.7% from the previous year), segment profit was ¥1,713 million (down 32.7%), and the number of transactions was 1,309 (up 10.3%). The securities report states that although the strengthening of sales staff and the sourcing of properties proceeded smoothly, retaining and training staff took longer than expected, causing a gap in the period from sourcing to sale, and fewer large-scale transactions than in the previous year, so results fell below the initial plan. From this fiscal year, the real estate brokerage business of House Do Housing Sales, which had been in the former "Real Estate Distribution" segment, is included in this segment.
entries.f349dd05fcbd0bd9: Real estate brokerage is the first business that led to the current House Do business. The company presents this history in its annual securities report as “History Before the Company's Establishment.”
entries.f6e89e0f7db644f0: It is a holding company. In January 2022, it changed its trade name from Hausudo Co., Ltd. and shifted to a holding company structure. The consolidated subsidiaries are Hausudo Jutaku Hanbai (Franchise Business), Hausudo Japan (Real Estate Sales Business), Financial Do (Financial Business), and Hausudo Hanbai Kanri and Keiyo Build (House Leaseback Business), five companies in total; Keiyo Build ceased to exist as of July 1, 2026 through an absorption-type merger with Hausudo Hanbai Kanri. The consolidated number of employees was 525 (temporary employees 111, as of June 30, 2026).
entries.f82ef70db2ad7651: A reportable segment that provides "House Leaseback," a service that lets customers sell their home while continuing to live in it. The Company buys the customer's property and enters into a lease agreement, and the customer can continue living there. The securities report describes it as a business that earns income gains from monthly rent and capital gains from future sale. For the fiscal year ended June 2026, sales were ¥9,521 million (down 50.9% from the previous year) and segment profit was ¥889 million (down 60.7%). In that year it newly acquired 172 properties and released 322 through transfers to funds, real estate trading companies and others, resale and disposal, and the cumulative number of properties held as of June 30, 2026 is 453. The securities report states that it scaled back this business during the fiscal year.
